title: Pinnacles earthquake downgraded to magnitude 5.0; 2 foreshocks and 15 aftershocks recorded

 Updated: 12:33 PM PST Nov 20, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Ricardo Tovar Digital Content Manager , Calif. — The U.S. Geological Survey now lists the earthquake that struck near Pinnacles at 10:49 p.m. Thursday as magnitude 5.0, down from its earlier preliminary estimate of 5.4. Shaking was felt as far as Marina.
 The quake was centered about 10 kilometers northwest of Pinnacles at a depth of 6.7 kilometers, according to the USGS. 
 Advertisement Two smaller quakes were recorded before it: a magnitude 3.1 at 9:53 p.m. and a magnitude 3.3 at 10:12 p.m.
 The USGS recorded 15 aftershocks, including a magnitude 3.4 at 11:14 p.m. Thursday and a magnitude 3.1 at 12:35 a.m. Friday. Other aftershocks ranged from magnitude 2.5 to 3.0 and were recorded at 10:52, 10:57 and 10:58 p.m.; 11:19 p.m., 11:21 p.m., 11:46 p.m., 11:57 p.m. and 11:58 p.m.; and 12:14 a.m., 12:25 a.m., 12:36 a.m., 2:49 a.m. and 7:07 a.m.
 A Marina resident said they received a USGS ShakeAlert and felt shaking. The alert advised people to “drop, cover, hold on” if shaking intensified.
 "Following the M5.0 earthquake near Pinnacles in San Benito County yesterday evening at 10:49 p.m., there are currently no reports of damage or injuries. Cal OES is actively coordinating with local authorities to evaluate any impact," said the California Governor's Office of Emergency Services.
